top_choice_rationale: P002 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) credits a mature discovery, 25 to 30 years old, that made government an endogenous actor. Electoral rules, constitutions, accountability and state capacity became objects of formal analysis with testable predictions about fiscal policy and public goods. Its attribution is the cleanest of the three award proposals, and Besley's state-capacity strand is separable enough to justify the third name. The citation can rest on the framework and not on contested cross-country constitutional-effect estimates. I judge the 2024 institutions prize a neighbouring but distinct discovery, since it asked whether institutions cause long-run prosperity and this work asks how rules inside a polity shape policy. I rank P001 second. Calvo, Taylor and Woodford is a defensible origin-of-ideas trio with the broadest policy reach, but it leaves out Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets, and the Taylor-rule and priority questions remain open. The choice between P002 and P001 is close and turns on weighing clean credit against breadth of influence. I rank P003 third because of the credit gap for Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, its proximity to the 2008 trade prize and Pareto-dependent welfare results. I rank P000 last because each proposal credits a mature, substantive achievement. Support counts are not treated as merit, and I have not independently verified citations or priority claims.
recusal_note: Field proximity, not adjudicated: my work on comparative democratisation, quality of government and state-building is close to P002's political-economy territory, so I guard against rating it on familiarity. No documented collaboration with Persson, Tabellini or Besley appears in my profile. My profile lists co-authored corruption work with 'Persson' and Rothstein, and which Persson is unresolved; I make no claim that it is Torsten Persson and do not rely on it either way. Torsten Persson is reported as an IIES colleague of committee members Hassler, Krusell and Boppart. I am in a different Stockholm University department from the IIES members and have no documented co-authorship with them. I was at Lund until 2021, where Kerstin Enflo, who also prefers P002, is based, and I have no documented co-authorship with her. None of the P001 or P003 credited names has a documented tie to me. My 2024 presentation speech does not establish a private preference.
